_comment: The exceptions to arthome-check-language, EACH WITH ITS REASON.
Everything committed to the repositories is written in English. French
survives in exactly two shapes, and both are CONTENT rather than interface
1. a VERBATIM COPY of the read-only design handoff. Translating it would
fork the copy from its source, and the copy is worth something only
because it is identical. Verified with cmp, not assumed.
2. the PRODUCT'S OWN VOCABULARY — discipline names, subgenres, tags, UI
copy. Arthome is a French-language product; its words are data.
Anything else is a file that has not been translated yet. Adding an entry
here to make the gate pass is the one use this file does not have.

allow.reason: The five design mockups, copied byte for byte from arthome-design/design_handoff_arthome/mockups/. Verified identical with cmp on 2026-09-21. They are the design, they are read only, and their French is the product's interface copy.

helpers.js, fixtures.js, catalogue.json, studio-data.js, i18n-compile.js — copied byte for byte from the handoff's shared/. Verified identical with cmp on 2026-09-21. The mission declares shared/ read only: it is the source the five surface specialists read, and a fork of it would be a second source of truth.
The French dictionaries themselves. Translating the French dictionary is a contradiction in terms.

The 21 disciplines, 176 subgenres and 205 tags are the product's vocabulary, carried verbatim by shared/taxonomy.json. Translating them here would create a second vocabulary that shared/ does not know — exactly fault E2, the parallel literal table, applied to a document.

_why: Inside prototypes/screens/**, the copy tables extracted from the mockups
are French and must stay French: they are the mockup's content, lifted
verbatim. The comments AROUND them are ours and must be English.
So the gate skips the extract blocks and checks everything else. A whole
file exempted would have exempted its header too, which is the part worth
checking.
A THIRD CATEGORY, and the only one that is not a file.
A record of why something was corrected quotes the thing it corrected, and
here that thing is often French. Translating the quotation destroys what it
is doing: "les quatorze entrées de navigation", translated, stops BEING the
defect and becomes a claim about one.
Neither file-level exemption covers this and neither should. The arbitration
log is written in English; exempting the whole file would exempt the prose
that is the point of it.
So an exemption names one QUOTATION, in one file, with its reason. Two
properties keep it honest: the text must appear VERBATIM in the file, so an
entry cannot widen into a blanket pass; and an entry whose quotation has gone
is an ERROR rather than a silent no-op, so it expires the day the sentence it
protects does.
If this list grows past a handful, the log has started quoting instead of
arguing.
An entry is a SINGLE-LINE fragment, because the check is per line. A quotation
that wraps needs one entry per line — which the gate told me on its first run,
about my own entry.

allow.quote: Le merch s'ajoute depuis la boutique d'un live
allow.reason: D-011. The mockup's own empty-state copy, quoted as the EVIDENCE that the cart carries merchandise and not seats — the finding that corrected an instruction I had given the surfaces. The arbitration rests on what the string says; a translation would be my paraphrase of the evidence rather than the evidence.

D-027b. A stale comment that said fourteen above a list of fifteen. The quotation IS the defect; translated it becomes a description of a defect, and the reader loses the ability to see that the count and the list disagreed.

allow.quote: nous on pourra faire de la
allow.reason: D-036. The project owner's own words, and the whole basis for treating automatic moderation as a STATED direction rather than an invented one — which is what distinguishes `automatic_filter` from a D-022 violation. A ruling that rests on what someone said must quote them, not summarise them. Wraps across two lines, so two entries.
